newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico offers banks help on foreclosed real estate.
newsitem.headline: Mexico offers banks help on foreclosed real estate.

text.p: The Mexican Banking and Securities Commission said on Wednesday it had established a five-year programme to allow banks holding foreclosed real estate assets to sell them to the government's bank support fund Fobaproa in return for promissory notes.

The programme "will allow, via trusts, the sale to Fobaproa of 70 percent of their foreclosed real estate assets and any given assets received in form of payment, at no cost to the federal government," the Commission said in a statement.
"Fobaproa will...issue a promissory note that will yield a rate equivalent to the 28-day TIIE nominal rate, capitalizing interest to maturity," it added.
The TIIE interbank interest rate, one of several reference rates used in the Mexican economy, is set weekly.

As the assets are sold by Fobaproa or by the banks on its behalf, the notes will be redeemed and after five years, those assets not sold will be returned to the banks unless Fobaproa decides to keep them, it said.
Any profits made in such operations will be shared by the banks and Fobaproa.
"Entries for up to 50 percent of the value of the assets will be registered in the financial statements as of the third quarter of this year," the Commission said.

"The purpose of this programme is to offer a reasonable amount of time...(for)...prices on real estate assets to recuperate, given that their current price is understated, thus promoting an orderly sale and avoiding an inconvenient impact on the current real estate market," the Commission said.

The banks offered the programme by the Commission are Bancomer, Banamex, Banca Serfin, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, Banco Mexicano, Banco del Atlantico, Banco Mercantil del Norte, Banco Internacional, Banca Confia, Banca Promex and Grupo Financiero Bancrecer's bank units Bancrecer and Banoro
